method.description: Actual source and all chronological contact sheets inspected using view_image. Evenly spaced frames include 0, 4 and last. CPU FFmpeg decoding, filtering and PNG encoding limited to two threads each; no GPU or generation submission.

observations: The green cactus with pink flower persists in every inspected sample, including frames 0, 4 and 123. It remains at the lower left without the previous disappearance.

Camel blinking, slight head/body bobbing and tail swaying are readable across chronological samples. Two humps, long neck, muzzle and four source legs remain coherent without abrupt sampled structural changes.
The cyan blanket, red border and three purple diamonds retain their structure and colours. No faces appear on the blanket, cactus or other non-animal elements.

The complete camel and cactus stay within the frame in the inspected samples, including the moving tail. Minor whole-composition bobbing is visible but no accumulating drift, clipping or sudden loss is observed.
limitations: Sampled still-frame inspection, not real-time playback or inspection of every frame. Motion observations describe progression across samples; frame-perfect smoothness, inter-sample artifacts and seamless looping are not guaranteed.
Contact sheets use reduced-size frames; full-resolution extracted samples are retained beside them.
scope: Exact-source and exact-video sampled visual reward-video review only. No painting processing, build, emulator, imports or integration performed or approved.
